title: When Text Misleads: Inconsistent-Aware Reasoning for Audio-Grounded Dialogue
abstract: arXiv:2608.27176v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Understanding spoken dialogue requires joint reasoning over lexical content and paralinguistic acoustic signals such as emotion and conversational intent. However, existing evaluations often allow shortcuts based on transcripts or single-modality solutions, obscuring whether models genuinely ground predictions in speech. We formalize this failure mode as cross-modal disagreement, where transcripts suggest plausible but incorrect surface interpretations while acoustic cues such as prosody or speaking style support different answers. We develop a scalable framework that identifies text-biased surface interpretations and converts disagreement regions into conflict QA examples. We also include consistent cases where transcript-based and speech-grounded interpretations agree, enabling evaluation beyond adversarial audio dependence. This results in ContraTalk, a controlled benchmark containing 501 questions across five discourse dimensions: in

translated_title: 当文本误导：音频对话中的不一致感知推理
translated_abstract: 理解口语对话需要对词汇内容和副语言声学信号（如情感和对话意图）进行联合推理。然而，现有的评估往往允许基于转录文本或单一模态解决方案的捷径，这掩盖了模型是否真正基于语音进行预测。我们将这种失败模式形式化为跨模态不一致，即转录文本暗示了看似合理但错误的表面解释，而韵律或说话风格等声学线索则支持不同的答案。我们开发了一个可扩展的框架，用于识别文本偏见的表面解释，并将不一致区域转换为冲突问答示例。我们还包含了一致的情况，即基于转录和基于语音的解释一致，从而能够在对抗性音频依赖之外进行评估。这产生了ContraTalk，一个受控基准测试，包含五个话语维度中的501个问题：情感、意图、讽刺、强调和不确定性。
tldr: 本文提出了ContraTalk基准测试，通过跨模态不一致检测框架，系统性地识别并利用文本误导与语音线索之间的冲突，以评估模型在音频对话中是否真正基于语音进行推理。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces ContraTalk, a benchmark that systematically identifies and leverages cross-modal disagreements between misleading text and acoustic cues to evaluate whether models genuinely ground predictions in speech for audio-grounded dialogue.
